name: Cat Care Checklist
description: A cat care checklist organizing daily, weekly, and monthly routines that keep a cat healthy and happy.

items.text: Serve measured meals at consistent times and refresh water.
Scoop the litter box and check for anything unusual.
Offer interactive play to keep your cat active.
Spend calm time bonding and observing behavior.
Wipe up spills and keep feeding areas clean.
Check appetite, energy, and mood for changes.
Brush your cat's coat, more for long-haired breeds.
Wash bedding and clean food and water bowls thoroughly.
Fully change the litter and wipe down the box.
Check ears, eyes, and teeth for buildup or odor.
Inspect the scratching post and rotate toys.
Confirm ID tag and any escape-prone areas are secure.
Give parasite prevention for fleas and worms on schedule.
items.note: Follow your veterinarian's recommended products and timing.

items.text: Weigh your cat and note any changes.
Trim nails if they have grown too long.
Review and refill any medications or supplements.
Restock food, litter, and supplies before they run out.
Confirm microchip and ID details are current.
Feed a quality, age-appropriate cat food in measured portions.
Provide clean, fresh water and encourage hydration.
Limit treats and avoid foods toxic to cats.
Transition any food change gradually over several days.
Adjust portions for age, weight, and activity.
Note appetite changes or vomiting for your vet.
Keep litter boxes clean, accessible, and away from food.
Provide enough boxes for a multi-cat home.
Watch for changes in urine, stool, or box use.
Clean around feeding and litter areas regularly.
Check coat and skin for fleas, mats, and lumps.
Maintain dental care as your vet recommends.
Keep up with routine wellness exams and vaccinations.
Watch energy, appetite, weight, and litter habits.
Give prescribed medications exactly as directed.
Provide perches, enrichment, and safe scratching outlets.
Keep emergency vet contacts handy.
Important: This is general information, not veterinary advice. Always consult a veterinarian about your cat's health, diet, and medications.

faq.q: What does daily cat care involve?
faq.a: Daily cat care means measured meals and fresh water, scooping the litter box, interactive play, and a quick check of mood and behavior. This cat care checklist groups these so the essentials happen every day.

faq.q: How often should I clean the litter box?
faq.a: Scoop the litter box at least once a day and fully change the litter regularly, cleaning the box itself periodically. A clean box encourages good habits and helps you notice changes in your cat's urine or stool that may warrant a vet visit.

faq.q: How often should I groom my cat?
faq.a: Most cats benefit from regular brushing, more often for long-haired breeds, plus occasional nail trims and dental care. Brushing reduces hairballs and shedding and lets you check skin and coat. Ask your veterinarian about a routine for your cat.

faq.q: How is this different from the new cat checklist?
faq.a: This cat care checklist is the ongoing daily, weekly, and monthly routine. Our New Cat Checklist covers settling a newly arrived cat into your home for the first time. Many owners use both together.

faq.q: Can I download this cat care checklist as a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. You can print it for the kitchen or download it as a PDF so the whole household can keep your cat's daily, weekly, and monthly care consistent.
